title: Third Mughal Emperor — Akbar the Great
summary: Jalaluddin Muhammad Akbar was the third Mughal emperor and one of the most celebrated rulers in Indian history. Known for his policy of religious tolerance, administrative genius, and patronage of arts, he expanded the Mughal Empire across most of the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Birth of Akbar
events.description: Akbar was born on October 25, 1542 at Umarkot Fort in Sindh while his father Humayun was in exile. He grew up in difficult circumstances during the tumultuous period of Mughal restoration.

events.title: Accession to the Throne
events.description: At just 13 years old, Akbar was crowned emperor at Kalanaur after his father Humayun's sudden death. Bairam Khan served as his regent during the early years.

events.title: Second Battle of Panipat
events.description: Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan decisively defeated Hemu's army at the Second Battle of Panipat, securing Mughal control over northern India.

events.title: Conquest of Chittorgarh
events.description: Akbar besieged and captured the mighty Chittorgarh Fort from the Rajputs after a prolonged siege, demonstrating Mughal military supremacy in Rajasthan.

events.title: Construction of Fatehpur Sikri
events.description: Akbar built the magnificent city of Fatehpur Sikri as his new capital, blending Hindu and Islamic architectural styles. It served as the Mughal capital until 1585.

events.title: Introduction of Din-i-Ilahi
events.description: Akbar founded Din-i-Ilahi, a syncretic religious philosophy blending elements from Islam, Hinduism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism, reflecting his pursuit of religious harmony.

events.title: Conquest of Kashmir
events.description: Akbar annexed Kashmir into the Mughal Empire, captivated by its beauty. He visited the valley multiple times and called it 'paradise on earth.'

events.title: Conquest of Sindh & Balochistan
events.description: Akbar extended Mughal control to Sindh and Balochistan, expanding the empire's western frontiers to the Arabian Sea.

events.title: Death at Agra
events.description: Akbar died on October 27, 1605 at Agra Fort at the age of 63. He was buried at Sikandra near Agra. His reign of 49 years transformed India's political and cultural landscape.
